name: Small merchant on a platform
oneLine: Wants agent sales with near-zero integration work and no new fraud.
goals: Turn on agent checkout from the platform dashboard (Shopify, Etsy, Wix) without hiring a developer.
Keep the order in the same system as every other order, with the same shipping and returns flow.
Get paid at the usual rate and settlement time, with no new fee line for agent orders.
Know which orders came from an agent so support can answer customer questions.
Avoid a rise in chargebacks or bot abuse because agents are now allowed in.
pains: Agent orders arrive with a token the merchant did not see created, so when a customer disputes one, the merchant has little evidence of consent.
Some platforms enroll merchants in agent checkout automatically, and the merchant learns about it from a customer.
Bot management rules that keep scrapers out also block legitimate shopping agents, and the merchant cannot tell them apart.
The DTVC path lets agents fill ordinary card forms, which looks like card testing in fraud tools.

No agent-specific dispute reason codes are published by Visa or Mastercard (as of 2026-10-21; Mastercard's Agent Pay Program Standards are not public), so an agent error is handled as a regular dispute.
decisions: Whether to opt in to the platform's agent checkout or stay out until liability is clearer.
Whether to allow agents to browse only, or to browse and buy.
Which bot-management setting to run: block unknown bots, allow verified agents, or allow all.
Whether an agent order gets extra review before shipping.
